question: In medical storage, what does the FEFO rule stand for?

options.A: First-Expired, First-Out
options.B: Fast-Entry, Fast-Output
options.C: Forward-Examination, Final-Order
options.D: First-Evaluated, Freight-Out

explanation: You nailed it! FEFO means items closest to their expiry date get used first so nothing goes to waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T12#GNS122_U3_T12_h6)

question: What is the most important thing to look at when choosing a research design?

options.A: The nature of the research question
options.B: The color of the hospital ward walls
options.C: The personal hobby of the lead nurse
options.D: The brand of computer in the office

explanation: Spot on! Your research question is the boss—it tells you whether you need an experiment, a survey, or an interview study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T2#GNS224_U1_T2_h7)

question: A family caregiver caring for an advanced cancer patient at home appears exhausted, irritable, and states they have not slept through the night in weeks. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Discuss options for respite care to give the caregiver a temporary break
options.B: Tell the caregiver that exhaustion is simply part of the job
options.C: Arrange for emergency placement of the patient in a permanent nursing home
options.D: Advise the caregiver to stop giving pain medications at night

explanation: Respite care provides temporary relief for exhausted family caregivers, preventing burnout and protecting their own physical and mental health. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h5)

question: What is a common nutrition mistake people make when switching to packaged gluten-free foods?

options.A: Consuming too much natural protein from fresh fruits and vegetables
options.B: Eating too many processed substitutes lacking fiber and B vitamins
options.C: Developing an immediate intolerance to all dairy products
options.D: Suffering from severe protein toxicity due to meat overconsumption

explanation: It's easy to rely on packaged gluten-free snacks, but many lack the fiber and vitamins found in whole or fortified foods. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of a preceptorship program for new nurses?

options.A: To make them work double shifts without extra pay
options.B: To test their memory with surprise written examinations
options.C: To pair them with an experienced nurse for guidance and support
options.D: To teach them how to manage hospital finances

explanation: Preceptors guide new staff through real clinical situations, helping them gain confidence and adjust smoothly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why do quality improvement teams prefer small-scale trials over massive, hospital-wide changes?

options.A: Small trials minimize patient risk and allow for quick adjustments
options.B: Hospital management bans large changes of any kind
options.C: Large changes require no documentation or staff meetings
options.D: Small trials are the only way to secure federal research grants

explanation: Starting small is a smart move! It protects patient safety and makes it super easy to tweak things if something isn't working quite right. [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h1)

question: What was the main focus of 'Selective Primary Health Care' introduced after the initial Alma-Ata momentum slowed?

options.A: Targeting specific, high-impact interventions for particular diseases
options.B: Stopping all vaccination programs to focus entirely on surgery
options.C: Handing over all health clinics to private international corporations
options.D: Building large multi-specialty teaching hospitals in every district

explanation: Selective PHC concentrated resources on specific, measurable disease interventions rather than broad, comprehensive health system building. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main trap when relying on routine blood tests to check mineral levels like calcium or magnesium?

options.A: Labs cannot measure minerals accurately in human blood.
options.B: Mineral levels change drastically every five minutes.
options.C: Blood levels may stay normal even when tissue stores are low.
options.D: Minerals break down instantly when exposed to room air.

explanation: The body is smart—it will pull minerals out of your bones and tissues to keep the blood levels looking normal, which can easily trick you! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T005#GNS227_U5_T005_h4)

question: A rural clinic notices a weekly increase in watery diarrhea during the rainy season. What should the nurses do first?

options.A: Ignore the data unless every single bed in the clinic is full
options.B: Close the clinic temporarily until the rainy season finishes
options.C: Wait until the end of the year to calculate annual averages
options.D: Report the trend upward to trigger quick public health support

explanation: Early reporting lets health authorities investigate water sources and rush supplies before things spiral into a full epidemic. You are thinking like a true public health nurse! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h7)

question: Which photoreceptor cells in the retina are responsible for sharp color vision in bright light?

options.A: Cones
options.B: Rods
options.C: Bipolar cells
options.D: Ganglion cells

explanation: Cones function best in bright light and provide detailed color vision. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the correct chronological order of the three stages in the General Adaptation Syndrome?

options.A: Alarm, exhaustion, resistance
options.B: Resistance, alarm, exhaustion
options.C: Exhaustion, resistance, alarm
options.D: Alarm, resistance, exhaustion

explanation: The body first experiences a sudden alarm, tries to resist the ongoing stress, and finally reaches exhaustion if the stress is too prolonged. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T6#GNS123_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is a very common reason why patients stop taking their prescribed medications?

options.A: Doctors instruct them to hide their medications
options.B: Pharmacies always run out of standard packaging
options.C: They start feeling better and assume they are fully cured
options.D: They prefer keeping pills in their original boxes

explanation: Many individuals mistakenly believe that feeling better means the underlying illness has completely gone away. Patient education is key here! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h6)

question: Why is taking a good patient history considered the bedrock of your clinical nursing practice?

options.A: It provides definitive proof of a medical diagnosis
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory investigations
options.C: It guides your physical assessment and care planning
options.D: It eliminates all risks of clinical documentation errors

explanation: Spot on! A thorough history points you in the right direction, helping you know where to focus your physical exam and how to plan the best care. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why must a laboratory result always be compared with the patient's physical condition?

options.A: Laboratory machines are always broken
options.B: Patients usually lie about their symptoms
options.C: Lab values alone do not tell the whole clinical story
options.D: Doctors refuse to read raw lab reports

explanation: A number on a lab sheet is only one piece of the puzzle and must match how the patient actually feels and looks. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T4#GNS124_U6_T4_h3)

question: What is the main goal of community mobilisation?

options.A: Empowering people to take action on their own health issues
options.B: Handing down medical instructions from government officials
options.C: Building large hospitals in rural and urban areas
options.D: Providing free prescription drugs to every household

explanation: Community mobilisation focuses on enabling local populations to identify and solve their own health challenges rather than relying entirely on outside help. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is another common name for a food-borne illness?

options.A: Bowel obstruction
options.B: Nutritional deficiency
options.C: Gastric influenza
options.D: Food poisoning

explanation: You've got this! 'Food poisoning' is simply the everyday term we use when someone gets sick from eating or drinking something contaminated. Keep going! [learn more](GNS227_U3_T010#GNS227_U3_T010_h1)

question: Which of these is a serious pregnancy danger sign that a mum must report right away?

options.A: Severe headache with blurred vision
options.B: Mild fatigue after moderate housework
options.C: Light swelling of the feet at the end of the day
options.D: Occasional mild heartburn after meals

explanation: A pounding headache and blurry eyes are huge red flags for preeclampsia. Catching this early prevents dangerous seizures! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T001#GNS226_U1_T001_h5)

question: Which tool is most commonly used for rapid neurological assessment in emergency settings?

options.A: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.B: Comprehensive mental status questionnaire
options.C: Deep tendon reflex chart
options.D: Full cranial nerve checklist

explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale provides a quick, reliable score for eye, verbal, and motor responses during emergencies. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which of these is a clear example of primary cancer prevention?

options.A: Starting chemotherapy for a diagnosed breast lump
options.B: Undergoing a routine screening colonoscopy
options.C: Receiving the Hepatitis B vaccine
options.D: Performing a monthly self-breast examination

explanation: Brilliant! Primary prevention stops a disease before it even starts. Giving vaccines against cancer-linked viruses like Hepatitis B is a classic way to protect the body early. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T3#GNS321_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main requirement for people chosen as 'cases' in a study?

options.A: They must be free of symptoms
options.B: They must be medical professionals
options.C: They must clearly have the disease
options.D: They must volunteer for the study

explanation: Spot on. To be a 'case', the person must actually meet the medical criteria for the specific condition we are investigating. [learn more](GST114_U2_T19#GST114_U2_T19_h2)

question: Which way of giving out a survey lets a nurse directly clarify confusing items for the respondent?

options.A: Anonymous drop-off boxes
options.B: Face-to-face administration
options.C: Unmonitored online web links
options.D: Standard postal mail surveys

explanation: When you are present during survey administration, you can immediately explain what a question means if the participant looks confused. Spot on! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h5)

question: In which hospital zone are people allowed to wear regular street clothes?

options.A: Semi-restricted zone
options.B: Restricted zone
options.C: Unrestricted zone
options.D: Sterile core

explanation: Correct! The unrestricted zone is the welcoming entrance area where street clothes are still fine before you move closer to the clean zones. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T1#GNS123_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common sign of a vulnerable individual facing forced marriage?

options.A: Sudden and unexplained withdrawal from school or work
options.B: Eagerly volunteering to travel abroad alone for vacation
options.C: Showing intense fear when a family member speaks for them
options.D: Unexplained physical injuries or signs of ongoing abuse

explanation: Victims are often coerced or taken abroad against their will, rather than eagerly volunteering for independent vacations. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h4)

question: A client on a weight-loss diet says they are always hungry and haven't lost any weight after four weeks. What should you do?

options.A: Tell the client to stop eating all solid food until the next appointment
options.B: Discharge the client from care for failing to lose weight
options.C: Review the current food intake and adjust the plan collaboratively with the client
options.D: Ignore the feedback because four weeks is not enough time to evaluate

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Sit down with the patient, figure out what's blocking progress together, and tweak the plan so it actually works for them. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of homeostasis in the human body?

options.A: Maintaining a stable internal environment
options.B: Speeding up cellular reproduction
options.C: Increasing muscle mass during exercise
options.D: Preventing all exposure to external bacteria

explanation: Homeostasis keeps vital internal conditions like temperature, blood pressure, and chemical balance within a safe, stable range. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h6)

question: Where would you expect to find an intramural fibroid?

options.A: On the outer surface of the uterus
options.B: Directly inside the uterine cavity lining
options.C: Inside the cervical canal
options.D: Within the muscular wall of the uterus

explanation: Think of 'intramural' as being right inside the walls—in this case, nestled comfortably within the muscular wall (myometrium) of the uterus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T22#GNS216_U5_T22_h3)

question: In nutrition, what does the term DRI stand for?

options.A: Dietary Restriction Index
options.B: Daily Recommended Instructions
options.C: Dietary Reference Intakes
options.D: Daily Routine Intake

explanation: DRIs are just the standard reference values health workers use to check if someone is getting enough nutrients. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h2)

question: Which of the following items should NOT be served on a soft diet?

options.A: Popcorn and potato chips
options.B: Well-cooked white rice
options.C: Mashed Irish potatoes
options.D: Smooth vanilla pudding

explanation: Hard, dry, and crunchy snacks like popcorn and chips can easily scratch the throat or cause choking on a soft diet. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h5)

question: Your patient just had shoulder surgery and is on bed rest. What is your next best move regarding AROM?

options.A: Encourage the patient to swing the arm rapidly to build strength quickly.
options.B: Check the medical orders and surgeon guidelines before allowing shoulder movement.
options.C: Ignore the surgery and start full arm rotations immediately.
options.D: Refuse to let the patient move any part of their entire body.

explanation: Always check the surgeon's rules first after an operation to make sure you protect the healing surgical site. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the main job of the posterior pituitary gland?

options.A: It breaks down worn-out hormones in the bloodstream
options.B: It stores and releases hormones produced by the hypothalamus
options.C: It manufactures tropic hormones for the adrenal glands
options.D: It controls blood calcium levels using direct neural input

explanation: The posterior pituitary acts like a warehouse—it doesn't make hormones itself, but safely stores and releases them when needed. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T4#GNS211_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why must a patient who has hit their head during a fall remain on the floor until help arrives?

options.A: Moving them could worsen hidden head or spinal trauma
options.B: It prevents the patient from feeling embarrassed
options.C: Floor surfaces are cooler for treating concussions
options.D: Hospital policy forbids touching patients after head trauma

explanation: Uncontrolled movement after a fall involving the head or neck can aggravate potential fractures or brain injuries. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h6)

question: How do EMR systems help stop medication mistakes compared to old paper charts?

options.A: By eliminating the problem of misreading messy handwriting
options.B: By automatically administering drugs without nurse approval
options.C: By letting patients prescribe their own medication at home
options.D: By completely removing the need for doctors to write orders

explanation: We've all squinted at difficult handwriting! Clear digital text keeps patients safe by taking the guesswork out of doctor's orders. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h1)

question: How can a nurse researcher best cut down on sampling bias?

options.A: Keep the sample size as small as possible to save time
options.B: Use random selection methods and clear inclusion criteria
options.C: Select only friends and family members who agree to participate
options.D: Ignore patients who do not fit the desired research outcome

explanation: You got it! Randomization and clear rules about who can join keep things fair and help your sample truly represent the wider population. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h6)

question: Why might a cancer care plan shift from trying to cure the disease to focusing purely on comfort and palliation?

options.A: Standard surgical options are suddenly much safer than outpatient chemotherapy.
options.B: The patient's insurance policy has expired and can no longer cover active medications.
options.C: The nursing staff prefers managing comfort care over administering toxic drugs.
options.D: The disease has progressed beyond the point where a cure or control is realistically achievable.

explanation: Spot on! When the disease advances past where treatment can stop it, the healthcare team shifts gears to palliation—focusing entirely on comfort, symptom relief, and quality of life. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T8#GNS321_U1_T8_h1)

question: A patient with HIV can stay healthy and symptom-free for years. What is happening inside their body during this time?

options.A: The virus replicates slowly while the immune system gradually loses ground.
options.B: CD4+ cells are multiplying faster than the virus can destroy them.
options.C: The virus has completely left the body's bloodstream.
options.D: Antibodies have cured the infection permanently.

explanation: Spot on! Even when a patient feels completely fine during the chronic phase, the virus is quietly at work, slowly wearing down their CD4+ cells. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h3)

question: Which medication is the standard, go-to antidote for a paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Atropine
options.B: Flumazenil
options.C: Naloxone
options.D: Acetylcysteine

explanation: You'll see this often in practice! Acetylcysteine saves the liver by restocking glutathione, which neutralizes the toxic breakdown products of paracetamol. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h7)

question: An activity coordinator plans a group exercise session. Which client adaptation best demonstrates person-centered care?

options.A: Excusing clients from participating if they look tired once
options.B: Requiring all clients to stand and follow the exact same routine
options.C: Skipping physical exercise altogether for safety reasons
options.D: Providing seated chair exercises for clients with poor balance

explanation: Adapting activities to individual functional levels, such as offering seated options, ensures safe and inclusive participation for everyone. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is the standard first-line treatment given to pregnant women with iron deficiency anaemia?

options.A: High-dose intravenous antibiotics
options.B: Routine whole blood transfusions
options.C: Oral iron supplements
options.D: Intramuscular vitamin B12 injections

explanation: Simple and effective! Oral iron tablets are the go-to first step in antenatal clinics to help build back the mother's iron stores safely. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T020#GNS226_U2_T020_h7)

question: How does data integration help prevent patient emergencies?

options.A: By sending text messages directly to the patient's family members
options.B: By combining multiple vital signs to catch subtle signs of decline early
options.C: By stopping nurses from having to check vital signs manually ever again
options.D: By letting machines make all medical diagnoses without human help

explanation: Looking at combined trends helps nurses intervene before a minor issue becomes a major emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which tool is commonly used to gather data in a correlational nursing study?

options.A: Standardized questionnaires and chart reviews
options.B: Active laboratory manipulation of patient blood pressure
options.C: Randomized drug trials on healthy volunteers
options.D: Surgical removal of tissue samples

explanation: Exactly! Since we aren't running lab experiments, we rely on surveys, scales, and looking at medical records to gather our facts. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T12#GNS224_U1_T12_h4)

question: Where do bedside nurses usually get the best ideas for a research topic?

options.A: Personal financial investment reports
options.B: Ancient historical nursing textbooks
options.C: Fictional medical television dramas
options.D: Daily clinical observations and ward routines

explanation: Your time on the ward is a goldmine! Noticing what gives patients trouble during your daily shift is the number one way to find real research topics. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T2#GNS217_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why should children with viral infections like chickenpox or flu never be given aspirin?

options.A: It causes severe green discoloration of the teeth
options.B: It completely stops the heart from beating
options.C: It is linked to Reye's syndrome, a dangerous brain and liver condition
options.D: It has no effect on pediatric fevers

explanation: Aspirin during viral illnesses can trigger Reye's syndrome—a rare but severe condition affecting the brain and liver. Always choose paracetamol instead! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T6#GNS215_U6_T6_h7)

question: Why are hospitals and clinics often the first places to spot survivors of gender-based violence?

options.A: It is usually the first safe haven where survivors seek help
options.B: Hospitals are legally required to solve all domestic disputes
options.C: Nurses have legal authority to arrest the perpetrators immediately
options.D: Medical facilities provide permanent housing for all affected persons

explanation: Spot on! When patients need medical attention for injuries, healthcare settings often become the very first safe space where they can quietly reach out for help. You're building great clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS312_U4_T10#GNS312_U4_T10_h1)

question: What is a major barrier to price transparency in many healthcare markets?

options.A: Patients are legally barred from asking about expenses
options.B: Hospitals update their price lists every minute
options.C: Final costs are often hidden or unknown until after treatment
options.D: All medical treatments cost the exact same amount globally

explanation: Opaque billing and complex negotiations make it very difficult for patients to know service costs upfront. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which side effect is very common with progestin-only injectable contraceptives (like Depo-Provera)?

options.A: Permanent complete hair loss
options.B: Changes in menstrual bleeding patterns
options.C: Sudden swelling of the thyroid gland
options.D: Instant weight loss of 20kg

explanation: Correct! Injectables often change how periods look—some spotting, heavier days, or periods stopping completely are quite normal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h6)

question: A nurse wants to run a malaria campaign. Which action shows great audience segmentation?

options.A: Creating one message for pregnant mothers and a separate message for community elders
options.B: Handing out the exact same flyer to every single person in the market square
options.C: Writing a medical journal article about malaria parasites for local farmers
options.D: Speaking only to the village chief and expecting him to tell everyone else

explanation: Audience segmentation simply means tailoring your message to fit different groups in the community. Pregnant mums have different needs than elders, so your approach should match! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T7#GNS124_U5_T7_h3)

question: Which area in the TSSU uses negative air pressure?

options.A: Preparation zone
options.B: Decontamination zone
options.C: Sterile storage zone
options.D: Packaging zone

explanation: Spot on! The dirty (decontamination) zone has negative air pressure so that air flows inward, trapping germs and stopping them from floating out into cleaner rooms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h2)

question: A patient with a bacterial infection wants to stop taking antibiotics after two days because they feel fine. What should you tell them?

options.A: They must double the remaining dose on the third day instead
options.B: They should save the remaining pills for a headache next week
options.C: Stopping early can cause the infection to return stronger and more resistant
options.D: It is completely safe to stop once fever symptoms disappear

explanation: You got it! Always encourage patients to finish the full dose so the infection doesn't bounce back stronger. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T6#GNS215_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is keeping the call bell right next to the patient so important for safe bathroom care?

options.A: It controls the room lighting and temperature automatically
options.B: It allows the patient to call for help before attempting risky, unassisted bathroom trips
options.C: It stops the patient from ever needing a bedpan during the night shift
options.D: It ensures the nurse can check the patient's telephone messages quickly

explanation: A reachable call bell is a fall-prevention tool! It reminds patients they don't have to struggle alone and encourages them to call you instead of risking a dangerous fall. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why is pregnancy particularly tough on a teenage bride's physical body?

options.A: Her body is still growing and competes with the fetus for nutrients
options.B: Adult nutritional requirements no longer apply to her body
options.C: Her immune system completely shuts down during gestation
options.D: Hormonal changes stop her bones from ever healing properly

explanation: Teenagers are still growing themselves! Their bodies need nutrients for their own development, which creates a direct competition with the growing baby. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T6#GNS225_U6_T6_h1)

question: Which of the following is classified as a barrier method of contraception?

options.A: Male and female condoms
options.B: Copper intrauterine device
options.C: Progestin-only injectable
options.D: Basal body temperature tracking

explanation: Condoms act as physical barriers that prevent sperm from entering the female reproductive tract. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h3)

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation is used only at home, while quarantine is strictly used inside hospitals.
options.B: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine restricts healthy people who were exposed.
options.C: Isolation applies to bacteria, while quarantine applies exclusively to viral infections.
options.D: Isolation requires wearing PPE, while quarantine requires taking chemoprophylaxis.

explanation: Remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick with an infection, while quarantine is for healthy people who were exposed and need to wait to see if they fall ill. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T2#GNS313_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient with an injury to their supplementary motor area would have the hardest time doing which of these?

options.A: Playing a practiced song on the piano from memory
options.B: Seeing a bright flashing light across the hospital room
options.C: Reflexively pulling a hand away from a hot stove burner
options.D: Feeling the texture of a piece of smooth velvet fabric

explanation: Playing an instrument takes smoothly linked, sequential movements—which is right up the SMA's alley! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T10#GNS211_U3_T10_h4)

question: What happens to perishable foods when transport infrastructure is poor?

options.A: They last much longer without refrigeration.
options.B: They spoil before reaching the market.
options.C: They become much cheaper to buy for villagers.
options.D: They turn into dry grains automatically.

explanation: Without good roads and cold storage transport, fresh foods easily rot before they can make the long journey to market. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h7)

question: A mum who is exclusively breastfeeding her 2-month-old baby asks about natural birth control. What is required for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) to work?

options.A: She must have experienced at least two normal menstrual cycles
options.B: She must practice exclusive breastfeeding and remain without menses
options.C: She must pump breast milk at least four times every night
options.D: She must supplement feeds with formula every night

explanation: LAM is a wonderful natural method, but it relies strictly on exclusive breastfeeding, a baby under six months, and no returned period yet. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h2)

question: Why is it so important to keep protein intake up while on a low-calorie diet?

options.A: To speed up quick water retention
options.B: To preserve lean muscle mass
options.C: To stop normal kidney filtration
options.D: To block all carbohydrate digestion

explanation: Well done! Eating enough protein gives your body the building blocks it needs so it burns fat instead of breaking down your hard-earned muscle. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T010#GNS227_U6_T010_h3)

question: When do hospital managers use a Cost-Minimization Analysis?

options.A: When evaluating the most expensive surgery available
options.B: When the outcomes of two treatments are completely unknown
options.C: When competing interventions produce identical clinical outcomes
options.D: When measuring patient satisfaction scores on the ward

explanation: If two drugs do the exact same job with the same results, you just want to find the cheapest one. That is what cost-minimization is all about! [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which body parts are included in the appendicular region?

options.A: Thorax and abdomen
options.B: Spine and pelvis
options.C: Upper and lower limbs
options.D: Head and neck

explanation: The appendicular region contains all the bones and soft tissues of the upper and lower extremities. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is a key safety step a home health nurse should take with a pregnant patient in case of an emergency?

options.A: Instruct the family to never call emergency services under any condition.
options.B: Encourage the patient to drive herself to the hospital if pain starts.
options.C: Establish a clear emergency plan and post local hospital numbers visibly.
options.D: Leave complex medical equipment in the home without instructions.

explanation: Having a clear, visible emergency plan ensures that family members can act quickly and correctly when urgent signs appear. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h8)

question: Which clinical setting uses an ambulatory EHR system?

options.A: An emergency trauma department
options.B: An intensive care unit monitoring drips
options.C: A hospital surgical recovery ward
options.D: An outpatient community health clinic

explanation: You nailed it! 'Ambulatory' means outpatient—think of local community health clinics where patients walk in and out the same day. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h2)

question: How many nurses must check the blood bag details against the patient's ID band?

options.A: Two licensed nurses
options.B: Only one registered nurse
options.C: Any available hospital staff member
options.D: A nurse and a laboratory technician

explanation: Two pairs of eyes are better than one! Having two qualified nurses check together is a mandatory safety net. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T18#GNS122_U1_T18_h3)

question: What do we call an infection that a patient picks up while receiving care in a hospital?

options.A: An allergic reaction to medication given during a surgical procedure
options.B: A chronic disease that worsens over many years of outpatient visits
options.C: Any illness a person brings into the hospital from their home environment
options.D: An infection a patient catches while inside a medical facility for care

explanation: You got it! These are known as healthcare-associated infections (HAIs), meaning they weren't there when the patient first arrived. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of primary prevention in healthcare?

options.A: Stopping health problems before they ever start
options.B: Screening for early signs of hidden cancer
options.C: Rehabilitating patients after a major stroke
options.D: Treating advanced chronic diseases with surgery

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on risk reduction and health education to prevent a condition from developing in the first place. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h4)

question: A hospital organizes a workshop on infection control. What result best proves the training actually worked?

options.A: An increase in the number of positive comments written about the guest speaker
options.B: A higher attendance rate compared to the previous hospital seminar
options.C: A larger collection of printed handouts left behind on the empty chairs
options.D: A noticeable decrease in hospital-acquired wound infections over the next month

explanation: When infection rates drop, it proves the nurses didn't just listen—they went back to the ward and put those safety practices into action! [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h5)

question: What is the main difference between equality and equity in healthcare?

options.A: Equity applies only to urban hospitals, while equality applies strictly to rural health posts
options.B: Equality gives everyone the same resources, while equity gives extra support to those with greater needs
options.C: Equity is decided by federal policies, while equality is managed by local community leaders
options.D: Equality focuses on curing diseases, whereas equity focuses entirely on disease prevention

explanation: Exactly! Equity recognizes that people start from different places, so we must distribute resources fairly based on actual needs to achieve true health for all. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h3)

question: A nurse wants to test if a new handwashing technique actually lowers ward infection rates. What study design fits best?

options.A: Historical biography
options.B: Qualitative phenomenology
options.C: Philosophical essay
options.D: Quantitative experimental

explanation: Because you are tracking numbers (infection rates) and testing an intervention, you need a quantitative experimental approach! [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h6)

question: Which mental health challenges commonly first show up during the adolescent years?

options.A: Depression and anxiety
options.B: Parkinson's tremors
options.C: Senile cataracts
options.D: Dementia and delirium

explanation: Spot on! Adolescence comes with massive life changes, making it a peak time for mood and emotional shifts like depression and anxiety to emerge. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h2)

question: You walk into a patient's room who has a new tracheostomy and notice thick green discharge and redness around the hole (stoma). What should you suspect?

options.A: Normal healing process
options.B: Accidental tube decannulation
options.C: A local stoma infection
options.D: Over-inflation of the cuff

explanation: Green, pus-like discharge and redness are classic warning signs of a bacterial infection at the site. Always report this and keep the area clean! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h4)

question: A patient is given naloxone to wake them up and reverse a dangerous morphine overdose. What kind of drug action is this?

options.A: Absorption
options.B: Potentiation
options.C: Antagonism
options.D: Synergism

explanation: Spot on! Naloxone acts as a true antagonist—it rushes to the rescue, kicks the morphine off the receptors, and blocks its effects to save the patient. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is 'click fatigue' in the context of electronic health records?

options.A: Physical hand cramps caused by holding a computer mouse too tightly
options.B: Spending excessive time navigating confusing menus and clicking through screens
options.C: A battery failure in wireless barcode scanners during night shifts
options.D: Eye strain from staring at bright computer monitors all day

explanation: Click fatigue happens when poor software design forces clinicians to perform too many clicks to complete simple documentation tasks. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which nursing theory focuses heavily on helping a person or community practice self-care?

options.A: Florence Nightingale's Environmental Theory
options.B: Dorothea Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory
options.C: Sigmund Freud's Psychosexual Theory
options.D: Abraham Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs

explanation: Spot on! Orem's model is all about empowering people with the skills they need to take charge of their own health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T7#GNS225_U2_T7_h6)

question: A patient refuses malaria treatment because they feel the drugs are too expensive and far away. In the Health Belief Model, what is this called?

options.A: Perceived severity
options.B: Perceived barriers
options.C: Perceived benefits
options.D: Perceived susceptibility

explanation: Perceived barriers are the hurdles, costs, or inconveniences that make someone hesitant to take healthy actions. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T1#GNS124_U5_T1_h5)

question: Which injection is routinely given to newborns to prevent bleeding?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Magnesium sulfate
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin C

explanation: Great job! Babies are born with low vitamin K levels, so this shot protects them from bleeding problems. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T15#GNS324_U5_T15_h5)

question: What is existential distress primarily centered around?

options.A: Physical pain caused by bone metastasis
options.B: Side effects of chemotherapy and radiation
options.C: Inability to afford hospital admission fees
options.D: Questions about the meaning and purpose of life

explanation: Existential distress involves deep worries about life's value, legacy, and the reason for suffering. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h3)

question: What is Manual Vacuum Aspiration (MVA) mainly used for in post-abortion care?

options.A: Safely emptying the uterus of retained products of conception
options.B: Inducing long-term hormonal contraception to prevent pregnancy
options.C: Suturing cervical lacerations caused by traumatic instrumentation
options.D: Delivering strong intravenous antibiotics to treat pelvic sepsis

explanation: Exactly! MVA uses a safe, specialized syringe system to quickly clear out the uterine cavity during early pregnancy complications. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h3)

question: Which antibody class is the main driver behind severe allergic reactions like anaphylaxis?

options.A: Immunoglobulin E
options.B: Immunoglobulin G
options.C: Immunoglobulin A
options.D: Immunoglobulin M

explanation: Think of IgE as the trigger-happy antibody! In anaphylaxis, IgE binds to mast cells and sets off a massive allergic chain reaction. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT allowed when conducting ethical nursing research?

options.A: Forcing patients to participate to get a large sample size
options.B: Protecting the privacy and confidentiality of patients
options.C: Ensuring participants are protected from physical harm
options.D: Obtaining informed consent from every participant

explanation: Participation in research must always be totally voluntary. Patients should never feel pressured or forced to join! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T4#GNS217_U3_T4_h4)

question: In a reflex arc, which part is responsible for catching the very first sign of trouble (like heat or pressure)?

options.A: Effector
options.B: Integration center
options.C: Motor neuron
options.D: Receptor

explanation: You got it! Receptors are like tiny guards in your skin and tissues waiting to pick up changes like heat, stretch, or pressure to kick off the reflex. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T25#GNS211_U3_T25_h2)

question: What makes Evidence-Based Practice (EBP) broader than just research utilization?

options.A: It completely ignores published research studies
options.B: It is performed exclusively by doctors and hospital managers
options.C: It only focuses on expensive international clinical trials
options.D: It combines clinical expertise and patient values alongside research

explanation: Spot on! EBP is a wonderful team player approach—it blends hard research with your own clinical skills and what the patient actually prefers. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h2)

question: How can a fear of side effects lead to drug under-prescription?

options.A: Doctors prescribe double doses to prevent side effects
options.B: Providers choose to omit necessary treatments to avoid potential harm
options.C: Patients stop buying drugs that cause mild stomach upset
options.D: Pharmacists refuse to fill prescriptions for elderly patients

explanation: Exactly! Sometimes being overly scared of side effects stops a practitioner from starting a drug that could actually do the patient a lot of good. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T8#GNS215_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why does the tissue lining the urethra change from transitional cells near the bladder to tough squamous cells near the opening?

options.A: Different tissues are required to filter bacteria out of the urine stream.
options.B: The external opening needs tougher tissue to protect against friction and environmental exposure.
options.C: The cells near the outside must produce mucus to lubricate the reproductive tract.
options.D: Changes in urine acidity destroy transitional cells as the fluid travels downward.

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Tough squamous cells protect the outer opening from daily wear and tear. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h4)

question: When checking a postpartum mother's legs, what dangerous condition are you mainly screening for?

options.A: Deep vein thrombosis
options.B: Peripheral neuropathy
options.C: Gestational hypertension
options.D: Calcium deficiency cramps

explanation: Because new mums sit or lie down a lot and their blood clots more easily after birth, we always check their legs for blood clots (DVT). [learn more](GNS226_U3_T012#GNS226_U3_T012_h4)

question: What is your safest immediate action if a mechanical ventilator suddenly stops working and you don't know why?

options.A: Disconnect the patient and ventilate manually with an Ambu bag
options.B: Turn off the machine and wait for a doctor to arrive
options.C: Increase the oxygen flow rate on the wall meter
options.D: Pull out the endotracheal tube immediately

explanation: Machines can glitch, but your patient needs oxygen right now. Grab the Ambu bag and ventilate manually while you call for help! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T5#GNS315_U3_T5_h6)

question: A postpartum mother has a tender, firm lump in one breast with mild redness, but no fever. What should the nurse suggest?

options.A: Encourage warm compresses, breast massage, and frequent nursing on the affected side.
options.B: Advise immediate cessation of breastfeeding and application of tight chest binders.
options.C: Administer a dose of oxytocin nasal spray to induce systemic breast involution.
options.D: Refer her urgently for a surgical biopsy to rule out malignancy.

explanation: This sounds like a blocked milk duct. Warmth, gentle massage, and keeping the baby feeding on that side will help clear the blockage right up. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h7)

question: What does a sudden, unexpected drop in the remaining volume of medication usually mean?

options.A: That the patient is metabolizing the drug much faster than usual
options.B: That the medication has expired inside the syringe barrel
options.C: A potential mechanical issue or free-flow of medication
options.D: Normal operation of the machine battery charging cycle

explanation: Spot on! If fluid disappears way too fast, stop and check right away for line leaks, programming errors, or accidental free-flowing. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T4#GNS212_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why must you always have a transport plan in place before attending a home birth?

options.A: It prevents wasting critical time when a sudden obstetric emergency arises
options.B: It removes the legal liability from the attending family
options.C: It guarantees that transport vehicles will arrive instantly
options.D: It ensures that normal births happen faster

explanation: Emergencies can pop up unexpectedly. Having vehicles and a hospital lined up beforehand means no scrambling or wasting precious minutes. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T3#GNS225_U3_T3_h6)

question: How should a washed diaphragm be stored after it dries?

options.A: In its designated storage case away from heat and sunlight
options.B: Wrapped tightly in a plastic bag inside the kitchen freezer
options.C: At the bottom of a handbag without any protective covering
options.D: Hanging openly on a bathroom wall hook exposed to light

explanation: Keeping it in its cool, dark storage case protects the material from heat and sunlight, helping it last a long time. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T017#GNS226_U6_T017_h6)

question: A high level of uric acid in the blood is a major clue for doctors diagnosing which condition?

options.A: Bone fracture
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Muscle atrophy
options.D: Gout

explanation: Gout happens when uric acid crystals build up in the joints. Checking blood uric acid is a fast way to spot it! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h3)

question: Why do we usually draw blood cultures from two different sites?

options.A: To reduce the pain experienced in one single arm
options.B: To help distinguish true infection from skin contamination
options.C: To speed up the laboratory processing time significantly
options.D: To collect a larger total volume of blood for testing

explanation: Drawing from two spots helps us know if bacteria in the bottle came from the patient's bloodstream or just from the skin during the poke. [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which sign shows mental fatigue in neurasthenia?

options.A: Sudden loss of consciousness
options.B: Uncontrollable muscle twitching
options.C: Poor memory and reduced concentration
options.D: Auditory and visual hallucinations

explanation: Great try! Mental tiredness directly affects your brain's ability to focus and remember things. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T9#GNS314_U2_T9_h2)

question: What is a major difference between normal postpartum blues and postpartum depression?

options.A: Postpartum blues resolve on their own within two weeks
options.B: Postpartum depression appears on the first day after delivery
options.C: Postpartum depression only affects women who had cesarean births
options.D: Postpartum depression require immediate psychiatric admission

explanation: The 'baby blues' are mild and usually fade away within a couple of weeks without special treatment, whereas postpartum depression is heavier, lasts longer, and needs real support. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h6)

question: Who is the main officer at the Local Government level in charge of gathering disease reports?

options.A: Chief Pharmacist of the Federal Teaching Hospital
options.B: Local Government Area Disease Surveillance and Notification Officer
options.C: National Minister of Finance and Budget Planning
options.D: Director of Immigration and Border Control

explanation: Spot on! The LGA DSNO is the key person coordinating surveillance and collecting initial reports from health facilities in the area. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h5)

question: A patient recovering from surgery suddenly complains of severe shortness of breath and sharp chest pain. What emergency should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: An infected leg ulcer
options.B: A pulmonary embolism from a dislodged blood clot
options.C: A blocked artery in the lower leg
options.D: Advanced Raynaud's syndrome in the fingers

explanation: Watch out for post-op patients! If a clot in the leg breaks loose, it can travel up to the lungs and block blood flow, causing sudden breathlessness and chest pain. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T10#GNS213_U1_T10_h5)

question: A nursing lecturer wants students to practice breaking bad news to a worried family member. Which method fits this best?

options.A: A standard lecture
options.B: Silent independent reading
options.C: Memorizing drug dosages
options.D: Role-playing

explanation: Role-play is brilliant for building communication and soft skills in a safe space before you ever have to face that situation with a real patient. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h3)

question: How does restrictive cardiomyopathy mainly affect the heart?

options.A: It thins out the walls until the heart bursts.
options.B: It makes the muscle rigid, preventing normal ventricular filling.
options.C: It causes the heart valves to dissolve rapidly.
options.D: It speeds up the electrical conduction pathways permanently.

explanation: In restrictive cardiomyopathy, the heart muscle becomes stiff and rigid. Because it can't relax, the chambers struggle to fill up with blood. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the main danger of feeding a severely malnourished patient too quickly?

options.A: Sudden permanent loss of all digestive enzyme production
options.B: Immediate development of chronic kidney stone formation
options.C: Dangerous drops in key electrolytes like potassium and phosphate
options.D: Rapid hardening of the major arteries in the neck

explanation: Sudden food intake shifts electrolytes into cells too fast, which can shock the heart if we aren't careful. Slow and steady wins the race here! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a positive sign of pregnancy?

options.A: Active movement felt by the examiner
options.B: Amenorrhea for two months
options.C: Fetal heartbeat heard on Doppler
options.D: Fetus visible on an ultrasound scan

explanation: Missing a period is a presumptive sign, not a positive one, because stress or illness can also stop menstruation. Only concrete proof like a heartbeat or scan is positive! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T002#GNS226_U2_T002_h4)

question: What is the main goal of doing an anthropometric assessment in nursing?

options.A: Measuring the size, weight, and proportions of the body
options.B: Assessing neurological reflexes and sensory function
options.C: Evaluating electrical activity within the heart muscle
options.D: Analyzing blood chemistry and electrolyte levels

explanation: You got this! Anthropometry is all about checking physical dimensions like height, weight, and skinfolds to see how healthy and well-nourished someone is. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T003#GNS227_U5_T003_h1)

question: Which hygiene practice should nurses advise patients to avoid to protect their cervix?

options.A: Using scented vaginal douches and chemical sprays
options.B: Washing the external vulva with plain warm water
options.C: Wearing loose-fitting cotton undergarments daily
options.D: Changing sanitary pads frequently during menstruation

explanation: Correct! Douching and scented products mess with the vagina's natural balance and easily irritate delicate tissues. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T16#GNS216_U5_T16_h7)

question: What is the big giveaway that a study is non-experimental?

options.A: The researcher does not manipulate any variables
options.B: Participants are randomly assigned to a treatment
options.C: A new drug is tested on a control group
options.D: Data is collected exclusively through interviews

explanation: Correct! In non-experimental studies, you just observe what is happening naturally without changing or meddling with anything. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which way of moving drugs across cell membranes needs the body to spend actual energy (ATP)?

options.A: Passive diffusion
options.B: Facilitated diffusion
options.C: Simple filtration
options.D: Active transport

explanation: Just like climbing a hill requires energy, 'active' transport uses cellular energy to pump substances across membranes, often against a flow. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T1#GNS125_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is a key piece of advice specifically for clients taking progestin-only mini-pills?

options.A: They completely stop all bleeding permanently
options.B: They must be taken at the exact same time daily
options.C: They must be stored in a refrigerator at all times
options.D: They require a backup barrier method for the first year

explanation: Mini-pills have a very short window of action. Taking them at the exact same time every day is key to keeping that cervical mucus thick and protective! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T011#GNS226_U6_T011_h3)

question: Why do people call the CPU the 'brain' of the computer?

options.A: It provides the physical screen display for viewing vital signs.
options.B: It processes instructions and performs calculations for running programs.
options.C: It permanently archives all patient records created in the hospital.
options.D: It connects the local hospital network to the wider internet.

explanation: Just like your brain does the thinking, the CPU does the heavy lifting by interpreting software instructions and running your apps. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T7#GNS113_U1_T7_h3)

question: A patient with a deep pressure ulcer is admitted to your ward. Why is increasing their protein intake so important for their care?

options.A: To cure any underlying bacterial pneumonia
options.B: To support collagen synthesis and tissue repair
options.C: To lower their overall daily caloric intake
options.D: To prevent the development of high blood pressure

explanation: Wounds need raw materials to close up. Protein provides the building blocks (amino acids) needed to grow new skin and heal tissue. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h3)

question: What is personal invulnerability in the context of adolescent psychology?

options.A: An advanced ability to resist peer pressure in all situations
options.B: The physical resistance to common sexually transmitted infections
options.C: A clinical diagnosis of complete emotional numbness
options.D: The belief that bad outcomes happen to others but never to oneself

explanation: Teens often think they are immune to pregnancy and infections, which leads them to take unnecessary risks with unprotected sex. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which complication is most likely to show up months or years after an untreated septic abortion?

options.A: Acute kidney failure needing dialysis
options.B: Severe allergic shock from local herbs
options.C: A sudden hole in the womb with bowel exposure
options.D: Infertility caused by blocked fallopian tubes

explanation: Scar tissue from past infections can permanently block the fallopian tubes, making it hard to get pregnant later. Brilliant nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h3)

question: How does an autoclave sterilize infectious waste?

options.A: By freezing the waste to extremely low temperatures
options.B: By soaking the waste in strong liquid bleach
options.C: By using high-pressure steam to kill pathogens
options.D: By crushing the waste into tiny metal cubes

explanation: Autoclaves use heat, moisture, and high pressure to destroy infectious microorganisms effectively before disposal. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h7)

question: Why is teaching new staff about infection control only on their first day not enough?

options.A: Hospital management changes policies every single week without fail
options.B: New nurses never listen to instructions given on their first day
options.C: Good habits fade and new safety guidelines emerge over time
options.D: Trainees are not allowed to touch patients until their second year

explanation: You got it! Regular refreshers keep safety fresh in everyone's mind as new guidelines come out. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h5)

question: Why is information science an essential pillar for nursing informatics?

options.A: It provides the ethical guidelines for bedside patient care.
options.B: It builds the physical computer towers used at the nurses' station.
options.C: It manufactures the electronic blood pressure cuffs.
options.D: It structures and organizes how clinical data is gathered and analyzed.

explanation: Information science specifically governs how data is organized, structured, and processed to make it meaningful for healthcare providers. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the main reason paracetamol (acetaminophen) is different from a true NSAID?

options.A: It causes severe stomach ulcers within hours of use
options.B: It can only be given through intravenous injection
options.C: It completely blocks both COX-1 and COX-2 permanently
options.D: It lacks significant anti-inflammatory properties

explanation: Paracetamol is great for knocking out a fever or a headache, but it doesn't do much for swelling or joint inflammation like ibuprofen does. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T4#GNS223_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is a major advantage of community-based rehabilitation programs in Nigeria?

options.A: They provide high-cost neurosurgeries in every primary health center
options.B: They bring essential therapy and support services closer to rural families
options.C: They completely replace the need for tertiary medical centers
options.D: They eliminate cultural beliefs regarding disabilities

explanation: Community-based programs bridge the gap for families who cannot easily travel to major city hospitals. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h6)

question: If a displaced community is staying in a crowded makeshift camp after a flood, what health threat should the nurse expect next?

options.A: Immediate reduction in baseline community trauma rates
options.B: Rapid spread of waterborne and communicable diseases
options.C: Sudden widespread outbreaks of genetic blood disorders
options.D: Total elimination of chronic lifestyle health conditions

explanation: When people are crowded together with poor sanitation, infectious diseases can spread very quickly. Nurses play a huge role in preventing this! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why does a good safety culture discourage hiding clinical mistakes?

options.A: Because nurses who make mistakes must be immediately suspended
options.B: Because patients always find out the truth through their medical records
options.C: Because hospital management requires public reports for every small incident
options.D: Because hiding errors prevents the team from learning and stopping repeat events

explanation: When staff feel safe reporting mistakes, the institution can analyze what went wrong and fix the system to protect future patients. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h1)

question: What is the core problem happening inside the body during all types of shock?

options.A: Inadequate tissue perfusion and cellular oxygenation
options.B: Rapid overproduction of red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: Sudden elevation in systemic arterial blood pressure
options.D: Excessive accumulation of bicarbonate in the blood

explanation: Shock means the body's tissues aren't getting enough blood flow and oxygen to keep the cells happy. It's an emergency requiring quick action! [learn more](GNS123_U1_T1#GNS123_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why do nurses and healthcare workers face unique safety risks on the job?

options.A: They face constant exposure to infectious agents and physical strain
options.B: They are completely immune to common hospital-acquired infections
options.C: They rarely interact with patients who have contagious diseases
options.D: They spend most of their working hours sitting at a desk

explanation: From lifting patients to handling needles and dealing with infections daily, nursing is physically demanding. Knowing this helps you protect yourself early! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h1)

question: Which blood pressure range is classified as Stage 1 Hypertension?

options.A: 140 or higher systolic or 90 or higher diastolic
options.B: Below 120 systolic and below 80 diastolic
options.C: 130-139 systolic or 80-89 diastolic
options.D: 120-129 systolic and under 80 diastolic

explanation: Stage 1 hypertension starts when the top number is 130-139 or the bottom number is 80-89. Good numbers to keep in mind for your clinicals! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h3)

question: Which of these hospital items is considered critical and needs full sterilization?

options.A: A surgical scalpel blade
options.B: A reusable blood pressure cuff
options.C: A stethoscope chest piece
options.D: A bedside plastic commode

explanation: Brilliant! Scalpels cut deep into sterile body tissues, so they must be 100% free of all germs and spores through proper sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h6)

question: If a vaccine gets ruined by heat, can it be saved by putting it back in the fridge?

options.A: Yes, within twenty-four hours
options.B: Yes, if shaken thoroughly
options.C: No, potency loss is permanent
options.D: Only if it is a viral vaccine

explanation: Once heat damages a vaccine's structure, you can't reverse it. It's always better to discard spoiled doses safely than give an ineffective shot. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h2)

question: What is the main reason a researcher tries to control variables in a study?

options.A: To ensure patients never experience any side effects
options.B: To make the research process as fast as possible
options.C: To isolate the specific effect of the intervention being tested
options.D: To hide unwanted data from the final report

explanation: Brilliant! Controlling variables helps you say for sure: 'Yes, this specific drug or nursing action is what made the patient better.' [learn more](GNS217_U2_T1#GNS217_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the most common type of primary heart tumour found in adults?

options.A: Papillary fibroelastoma
options.B: Rhabdomyoma
options.C: Myxoma
options.D: Angiosarcoma

question: What is the Hawthorne effect when observing staff nurses during audits?

options.A: A sudden spike in patient admissions during the rainy seasonal period
options.B: The mathematical formula used to calculate hospital bed occupancy rates
options.C: The rapid physical exhaustion nurses feel toward the end of a night shift
options.D: Staff changing their behavior temporarily because they know they are being watched

explanation: The Hawthorne effect reminds us that people naturally change how they work when they know someone is watching them closely. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h5)

question: Which professional is best suited to organize tricky medications into weekly blister packs for a patient?

options.A: Radiology technician
options.B: Laboratory scientist
options.C: Hospital accountant
options.D: Pharmacist

explanation: Pharmacists are medication pros! They love helping patients sort out tricky schedules using pill organizers and blister packs. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why must a nurse demonstrate the call bell system immediately upon a patient's arrival?

options.A: It distracts the patient from their current physical pain
options.B: It gives the patient a direct way to call for help when needed
options.C: It proves to the visiting family members that the equipment works
options.D: Hospital policy requires it to be tested every single hour

explanation: Showing the patient the call bell ensures they can easily summon assistance for urgent needs like using the toilet or managing sudden pain. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which mechanism allows one drug to help another enter cells more easily?

options.A: Destroying all circulating white blood cells
options.B: Altering cell membrane permeability
options.C: Increasing the patient's daily fluid intake
options.D: Speeding up normal kidney filtration rates

explanation: By changing how easy it is to pass through the cell membrane, one drug acts like an opening wedge, helping its partner medication get inside. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T6#GNS125_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which pancreatic hormone is primarily responsible for lowering blood glucose levels?

options.A: Cortisol
options.B: Thyroxine
options.C: Glucagon
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Insulin facilitates the movement of glucose out of the bloodstream and into body cells, effectively lowering circulating blood sugar levels. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h3)

question: A nurse draws up the wrong dose of insulin, but catches the mistake before giving it to the patient. What is this called?

options.A: A systemic failure
options.B: An adverse event
options.C: A sentinel event
options.D: A near miss

explanation: Spotting the mistake before the injection means no harm was done. That's a classic near miss—phew! [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h2)

question: How many distinct stages are there in complete metamorphosis?

options.A: Two simple stages
options.B: Five continuous stages
options.C: Three active stages
options.D: Four distinct stages

explanation: Complete metamorphosis is a total makeover! It goes through four steps: egg, larva, pupa, and adult. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h3)

question: What is a great way to reach people with low reading skills during a public safety campaign?

options.A: Posting complex legal notices online
options.B: Using visual aids and pictures
options.C: Relying solely on written email newsletters
options.D: Distributing dense academic textbooks

explanation: You got it! Pictures and clear demonstrations help share safety messages effectively with everyone in the community. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T10#GNS315_U5_T10_h4)

question: Why is patient stability so important when deciding whether or not to delegate a task?

options.A: Stable patients do not require any monitoring from healthcare workers
options.B: Unstable patients always pay more for hospital accommodation
options.C: Stable patients are harder to communicate with than unstable ones
options.D: Unstable patients require continuous clinical judgment that only a registered nurse can provide

explanation: When a patient's condition can change rapidly, it needs a professional nurse's close assessment rather than auxiliary care. [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h4)

question: What does 'asynchronous development' mean when talking about gifted children?

options.A: Language skills develop long before motor skills.
options.B: Physical growth happens much slower than in normal peers.
options.C: Intellectual, emotional, and physical ages do not match.
options.D: Emotional maturity always outpaces cognitive ability.

explanation: Exactly! Asynchronous just means uneven development. A child might have the mind of a 10-year-old, the emotions of a 6-year-old, and the body of an 8-year-old all at once. You're crushing this! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T1#GNS225_U5_T1_h3)

question: Which factor puts low-income city dwellers at higher risk during a disaster?

options.A: Owning multiple multi-story buildings downtown
options.B: Living in informal settlements located in hazard-prone zones
options.C: Working exclusively in high-level government offices
options.D: Having private helicopters for immediate evacuation

explanation: Spot on! Poverty often forces families to build homes in high-risk areas like floodplains where disasters hit hardest. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h4)

question: What is the happy result of successfully narrowing down your nursing research topic?

options.A: The complete elimination of all hospital illnesses
options.B: A specific, manageable question that can be investigated thoroughly
options.C: A massive textbook that covers every disease in medicine
options.D: An automatic guarantee of winning a research award

explanation: When you narrow your focus, you end up with a sharp, clear question that you can actually research, answer, and feel proud of! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T2#GNS217_U3_T2_h7)

question: How does public health differ from regular clinical (curative) medicine?

options.A: Curative medicine focuses on individuals, while public health focuses on communities.
options.B: Public health ignores infectious diseases completely.
options.C: Clinical medicine relies entirely on environmental sanitation.
options.D: Curative medicine is only practiced in rural areas.

explanation: You've got it! Clinical practice is all about treating the single sick person in front of you, whereas public health cares for the health status of the whole group. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h1)

question: Why is unmanaged variation dangerous in clinical practice?

options.A: It stops doctors from ever speaking with nursing staff
options.B: It leads to unpredictable patient care and higher error rates
options.C: It guarantees that all nurses will finish their shifts too early
options.D: It forces the hospital to buy expensive new computer systems

explanation: When everyone does tasks differently without a standard, quality becomes unpredictable and patient safety is compromised. That's why clinical guidelines exist! [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h4)

question: What major economic challenge often pushes desperate families toward child traffickers?

options.A: Widespread poverty and lack of basic needs
options.B: Abundant job opportunities in local markets
options.C: Strict government taxes on large families
options.D: Excessive wealth in rural farming villages

explanation: When families struggle to put food on the table, traffickers easily trick parents by promising money or a better future for their kids. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T25#GNS225_U5_T25_h2)

question: What makes contact tracing particularly tricky in many Nigerian rural areas or busy towns?

options.A: Strict laws that ban public health workers from making phone calls
options.B: Logistical hurdles, poor road networks, and misinformation
options.C: Complete lack of infectious diseases occurring in the country
options.D: An excess of trained nurses in every primary healthcare center

explanation: You got it! Bad roads, hard-to-reach villages, and false rumors can make tracking down contacts a real test of patience and resourcefulness. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h7)

question: What is considered the single most effective habit to stop the spread of infection?

options.A: Changing hospital scrubs hourly
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Wearing sterile gloves all day
options.D: Using strong chemical sprays

explanation: Good old handwashing (or using alcohol rub) at the right moments is your absolute best defense against spreading germs! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h8)

question: How is the autonomic nervous system different from the somatic nervous system?

options.A: The autonomic system is completely independent and never interacts with the brain.
options.B: The autonomic system controls involuntary organs while the somatic controls voluntary muscles.
options.C: The autonomic system only uses sensory neurons while the somatic uses motor neurons.
options.D: The autonomic system is located in the brain while the somatic is in the spinal cord.

explanation: Spot on! Somatic nerves let you move your arms and legs on purpose, while autonomic pathways handle the behind-the-scenes organs that work without your direct control. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T5#GNS211_U3_T5_h1)

question: A patient refuses to leave their house because they are terrified of having a panic attack in public and not being able to escape. What is this called?

options.A: Generalized anxiety disorder
options.B: Obsessive-compulsive disorder
options.C: Agoraphobia
options.D: Social anxiety disorder

explanation: You nailed it. Agoraphobia is the fear of being trapped in public spaces where escape feels hard, which often leads people to stay safely inside their homes. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h2)

question: As a nurse assessing patient movements, what do you call moving a limb away from the midline of the body?

options.A: Flexion
options.B: Abduction
options.C: Adduction
options.D: Pronation

explanation: Spot on! When you 'abduct' something, you take it away—just like lifting your arm up away from your side. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T6#GNS121_U3_T6_h7)

question: Two clinical supervisors watch the same nursing student perform a procedure and grade them using the same checklist. What are they checking?

options.A: Test-retest validity
options.B: Content consistency
options.C: Inter-rater reliability
options.D: Patient satisfaction

explanation: Inter-rater reliability checks whether different observers get similar scores when using the exact same tool. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of an Institutional Review Board (IRB) in research?

options.A: To provide financial grants and equipment to student researchers
options.B: To grade the academic performance of nursing postgraduate students
options.C: To market the finished research paper to private pharmaceutical companies
options.D: To protect the rights, safety, and well-being of human research subjects

explanation: An ethics committee or IRB reviews study proposals beforehand to make sure human participants will not be harmed or exploited. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why is it so important for a patient to stay completely still during an MRI scan?

options.A: Shifting positions triggers an automatic safety alarm in the control room
options.B: Movement blurs the scan and ruins the quality of the pictures
options.C: Patient movement interferes with the electrical wiring of the hospital
options.D: Moving too fast can cause the machine's magnetic field to shut down

explanation: Spot on! Just like taking a photo with a phone camera, moving makes the image blurry and hard for doctors to read. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h5)

question: What is the difference between client privacy and client confidentiality?

options.A: Privacy refers to hospital finances, whereas confidentiality refers to drug stock inventories
options.B: Privacy is a legal rule, whereas confidentiality is merely a personal suggestion
options.C: Privacy applies only to doctors, while confidentiality applies exclusively to nursing assistants
options.D: Privacy involves the client's body and physical space, whereas confidentiality involves keeping health information secret

explanation: Privacy protects physical boundaries, while confidentiality protects verbal and written medical data shared in professional trust. [learn more](GST321_U10_T5#GST321_U10_T5_h5)

question: In respiratory care, what does the term 'weaning' mean?

options.A: Lowering the room temperature to cool the patient
options.B: Gradually transitioning the patient back to spontaneous breathing
options.C: Stopping nutrition support to rest the stomach
options.D: Removing all medications from the patient's intravenous line

explanation: Weaning is like taking off the training wheels. As the patient gets stronger, we slowly reduce machine support so they can breathe on their own again. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T5#GNS315_U3_T5_h7)

question: What is the literal meaning of the word 'pons'?

options.A: Bridge
options.B: Tunnel
options.C: Pillar
options.D: Gateway

explanation: The term pons translates to bridge, reflecting its anatomical job of connecting different regions of the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h1)

question: Why is it important for nurses to understand food availability in the local community?

options.A: To teach patients how to manage supermarket finances
options.B: To trace nutritional deficiencies back to environmental supply issues
options.C: To calculate exact daily caloric needs for hospital patients
options.D: To inspect local restaurants for health code violations

explanation: Spotting why a community lacks food helps you connect a patient's poor health to wider supply problems outside their home. Great nursing insight! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T021#GNS227_U2_T021_h1)

question: Which of these is a primary prevention action in a community?

options.A: Rebuilding a hospital that was destroyed by an earthquake
options.B: Building a strong embankment to stop seasonal river flooding
options.C: Treating injured victims at a temporary field clinic
options.D: Providing counseling for survivors after a major fire outbreak

explanation: Great job thinking ahead! Primary prevention stops the hazard from causing harm before it even happens. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h1)

question: What do we call the tapered, cone-shaped lower end of the spinal cord?

options.D: Filum terminale

question: What is a major feature of employer-sponsored health insurance?

options.B: It is completely managed by the Ministry of Health
options.C: It is strictly limited to retired civil servants
options.D: It is provided by companies as part of worker compensation

explanation: Spot on! Employer-sponsored plans are job benefits where companies help cover or fully pay health insurance for their staff. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why should you avoid giving ergometrine to a mother with severe high blood pressure?

options.A: It triggers immediate and uncontrollable uterine relaxation
options.B: It completely stops all breast milk production permanently
options.C: It causes a dangerous spike in maternal blood pressure
options.D: It neutralizes the effects of routine postpartum antibiotics

question: Why can having a very small number of patients (sample size) ruin statistical conclusion validity?

options.A: It makes it hard for the math to catch real differences between groups
options.B: It makes the external validity way too broad
options.C: It automatically makes patients run away
options.D: It proves the whole theory is wrong

explanation: When your sample size is too tiny, statistical tests struggle to spot real changes, meaning you might miss an important finding. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T26#GNS224_U1_T26_h5)

question: Where should you position the lower edge of the blood pressure cuff on the patient's arm?

question: Why do specialty nurses, like nurse anesthetists, pay higher malpractice insurance rates?

options.C: Insurance companies charge extra fees for nurses who work night shifts

question: Which household practice comes from a misunderstanding about how HIV is spread?

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to keep a stakeholder coalition strong and unified?

options.D: Transparent communication among groups

question: A patient is given a medication with strong anticholinergic properties. As a nurse, what side effect should you watch out for?

options.C: Dry mouth and trouble urinating

question: Why does an HMO require a formal referral before a patient sees a specialist?

options.A: To give the patient something to do on weekends
