options.C: To ensure the specialist hospital gets less money from the pool
options.D: To control costs and ensure patients see the right expert for their condition

explanation: Gatekeeping prevents patients from bypassing basic clinics for expensive specialist care they might not actually need. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is the medical term for the physical act of swallowing?

question: Which joint is looked at most often using an arthroscope?

question: What is a typical role of a traditional priest when families seek help?

options.C: Providing formal university degrees in nursing
options.D: Manufacturing modern psychiatric medications in factories

question: A nurse notices that the cleaning staff plugged an electric kettle into the same socket used for the vaccine refrigerator. What should the nurse do?

question: Where is the body's center of gravity usually located when standing normally?

question: Which government tier is primarily responsible for managing Primary Health Care centers?

question: What triggers an outbreak investigation in a healthcare facility?

options.A: An unusual cluster of infections detected by surveillance
options.B: A routine check of fire extinguishers
options.C: The arrival of a new hospital director
options.D: The annual painting of the ward walls

explanation: Surveillance spots the abnormal rise in cases, which prompts a full investigation. [learn more](GST114_U2_T15#GST114_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is the safe minimum distance to keep portable heaters away from things like curtains and bedding?

question: What is the V-shaped groove on the tongue that separates the front two-thirds from the back one-third?

question: Where should a nurse record every vaccine dose right after giving it to a baby?

question: A nurse wants to refer a newly diagnosed, fearful patient to a support group. What is the best approach?

options.A: Leave a stack of group fliers on the waiting room table and say nothing
options.B: Discuss the patient's specific fears and explain what to expect at a meeting
options.C: Wait until the patient stops taking medications before mentioning any groups
options.D: Insist that attending the group is a legal requirement for getting medications

explanation: Effective referrals require personal guidance, addressing fears, and preparing the patient rather than just handing over a flier. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T7#GNS216_U6_T7_h5)

question: After how many months of trying to conceive without success do doctors officially define infertility?

options.C: Twelve months or more
options.D: Three months or less

question: Why does an overstretched, fibrous uterus struggle to stop bleeding after delivery?

question: Why does atrophic gastritis often lead to vitamin B12 deficiency in older adults?

options.A: It speeds up the digestion of vitamins before the body can use them

options.C: It destroys the bacteria in the gut that naturally manufacture B12
options.D: It causes the liver to store less vitamin B12 than normal

explanation: Spot on! When stomach acid and intrinsic factor drop, the body struggles to break B12 away from food and absorb it in the gut. Great nursing insight to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T014#GNS227_U2_T014_h1)

question: What is the main benefit of using an infusion pump instead of a normal gravity IV line?

options.A: It warms the intravenous fluid before it enters the vein
options.B: It completely removes the need to monitor the IV site
options.C: It delivers fluids at a precise and controlled rate
options.D: It prevents all forms of air embolisms automatically

explanation: Spot on! Infusion pumps give us exact control over how fast fluids run, which is much safer and more reliable than just relying on gravity. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T3#GNS212_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why do health coordinators analyze student clinic attendance records during a programme evaluation?

options.A: To punish students who visit the nurse too frequently
options.B: To calculate the exact salaries of the school nurses
options.C: To determine which textbooks are best for mathematics
options.D: To measure the success of preventive measures and identify trends

explanation: Clinic records reveal patterns of illness, helping teams evaluate whether health interventions are reducing disease incidence. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h8)

question: In community health, who do we usually refer to as 'stakeholders'?

options.C: Only foreign donors funding the health center
options.D: Patients who refuse to take prescribed medications

explanation: Stakeholders are simply all the key players—from local leaders and health workers to the residents themselves—who care about or are affected by the community's health. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h2)

question: A patient with a bad ankle sprain gets a short leg cast. What is the main goal here?

options.A: Enhancing rapid cartilage regrowth in the joint
options.B: Resting the injured joint to reduce inflammation
options.C: Removing excess fluid trapped inside the joint capsule
options.D: Preventing permanent muscle atrophy in the calf

explanation: By keeping the sprained joint still, you stop painful movement and give the damaged ligaments time to rest and heal. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T5#GNS221_U1_T5_h2)

question: How many fundamental questions form the foundation of the Model for Improvement?

options.B: Five

options.D: Ten

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended first step when managing challenging behaviors in dementia?

options.B: Reviewing the daily routine for sources of overstimulation
options.C: Playing soft and familiar background music
options.D: Looking for signs of physical pain or discomfort

explanation: Always start with non-drug approaches! Heavy meds carry serious risks and shouldn't be the first resort for everyday behavioral issues. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h5)

question: What happens if different nurses on the ward use their own personal definitions for something like a 'medication error'?

options.C: The data becomes unreliable and useless for tracking real progress

question: In healthcare quality improvement, what does "spreading" an idea mean?

options.A: Spreading a contagious disease from one patient room to another
options.B: Expanding the physical size of the hospital emergency department
options.C: Increasing the total number of nursing staff on every hospital shift
options.D: Taking a successful local change and sharing it with other units or facilities

explanation: You've got this! Spread simply means taking a great idea that worked well in one ward and sharing it so other care areas can benefit too. [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h1)

question: What do we call the thick, yellowish first milk produced right after birth?
